_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::contact#9 — a line search does not rescue a failing contact Newton, and the trace shows why: the step length never leaves 1.0, so the line search has nothing to shorten. Five runs of the failing two-block mortar penalty deck (-0.9 over ten steps, PENALTYPARAM 1e4, the same configuration contact#8 shows chattering), run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Observed: STRUCT NOX/Line Search Method set to Backtrack, Polynomial, Full Step and More'-Thuente gives four runs whose per-iteration (||F||, step, dx) traces are BYTE-IDENTICAL (TRACES_IDENTICAL_ACROSS_METHODS=yes), each with 55 lines reading 'step = 1.00000e+00', one finalised step and then 'The nonlinear solver did not converge!' from solver_nonlin_nox/4C_solver_nonlin_nox_problem.cpp. The only step lengths that ever appear are 0.00000e+00 (the predictor line of each time step) and 1.00000e+00 — STEP_LENGTHS_STRICTLY_BETWEEN_ZERO_AND_ONE=0, so no backtracking ever happens. The fifth arm rules out the obvious alternative explanation that the section is ignored: a bogus Method value is refused with 'Could not match this input' and never starts a solve (BOGUS_METHOD_STARTED_A_SOLVE=0), so 4C reads and honours the setting; it simply has no leverage on an active set that chatters. Shrink the time step instead.
expect_in_output: The nonlinear solver did not converge!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: shrink the prescribed displacement so every arm converges instead of chattering. The failure disappears along with the 55 unit-step lines and 'The nonlinear solver did not converge!', so the fixture must go red.
make the bogus arm legal. 'Could not match this input' disappears, so the fixture must go red.
